nodes.summary: There is a real constant $c > 0$ such that for every integer $k \ge 1$ there is an $N_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ such that for every $N \ge N_0$ and every colouring $f : \mathbb{N} \to \{0, \dots, k-1\}$, at least $cN$ of the integers $n \in \{1, \dots, N\}$ can be written as $n = a + b$ with $a, b \in \{1, \dots, N\}$, $a \ne b$ and $f(a) = f(b)$.
nodes.title: Erdős–Sárközy–Sós theorem on monochromatic sums (Erdős Problem 484)

nodes.summary: This is the statement that there is a real constant $c > 0$ such that for every integer $k \ge 1$ there is an $N_0 \in \mathbb{N}$ with the following property: for every $N \ge N_0$ and every colouring $f : \mathbb{N} \to \{0, \dots, k-1\}$, at least $cN$ of the integers $n \in \{1, \dots, N\}$ can be written as $n = a + b$ with $a, b \in \{1, \dots, N\}$, $a \ne b$ and $f(a) = f(b)$.
nodes.title: Erdős Problem 484: linearly many monochromatic sums
